summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for evaluation of leaking from his left nephrostomy tube, which began after a recent replacement during a prior hospitalization. He has a complex medical history including T12 paraplegia, chronic kidney disease stage IV, neurogenic bladder, and recurrent urinary infections. Imaging revealed a stricture at the ureteropelvic junction and near the ileostomy anastomosis, contributing to the leakage. The nephrostomy tube was successfully exchanged with a modified stent, resolving the leak. He was found to have asymptomatic bacteriuria with E. coli, which did not require treatment. His chronic metabolic acidosis improved with an increased dose of sodium bicarbonate, and his previously noted toxic metabolic encephalopathy resolved. Nephrology was consulted, and a follow-up appointment was scheduled to discuss future dialysis planning. He remained stable, with no signs of active infection or complications, and was discharged home in improved condition.
